comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C30-C33 regarding structural interactions between AR domain and TRP helix. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes FDA analysis and convergent evidence from prior work, while peer reviewers accept the findings but suggest experimental validation through mutagenesis would enhance the manuscript.

Perfect agreement on claims C50-C56 regarding force transmission and hydrogen bonding networks. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the quantitative PCC calculations and statistical evidence, while peer reviewers characterize the work as 'detailed, rigorous simulations' that add molecular detail to force transduction pathways.

Perfect agreement on claims C62-C65 regarding universality of TRP rotation across TRP channel subfamilies. Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the systematic comparative analysis and the HsTRPA1 exception, while peer reviewers emphasize the significance for the broader TRP channel family and potential implications for non-mechanically gated channels.

Disagreement on claims C68-C71 regarding TRP-S4-S5 composite unit functional role. OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are 'speculative proposals' requiring further investigation. Peer reviewers rate them as SUPPORTED, accepting them as reasonable hypotheses arising from simulation data without requesting additional evidence.

Disagreement on claims C72-C73 regarding TRPV1 simulations and AR domain role. OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN due to preliminary nature and acknowledged uncertainty about biological relevance in mammalian channels. Peer reviewers rate them as SUPPORTED, accepting the findings as evidence for broader applicability of the torsional gating mechanism.

Both address structural changes and force distributions (C26-C29) from FDA analysis. OpenEval finds claims C24-C29 SUPPORTED with emphasis on quantitative characterization. Peer reviewers find C26-C29 SUPPORTED, describing simulations as 'detailed, rigorous' and noting they quantify forces for subsequent experiments. OpenEval R1 also covers C24-C25 which peer reviewers address separately in R9.

Both address compression-twist coupling (C43-C48). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED based on quantitative analysis from trajectory RII. Peer reviewers also find them SUPPORTED (C43-C45, C47-C48 in their R2), describing it as a 'valuable finding' about torsional force transmission and treating compression-twist coupling as a supporting mechanistic detail.

Major disagreement on claims C34-C40 regarding differential effectiveness of force components. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED by systematic simulation experiments with quantitative pore size and water permeation data. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging it as the 'most important finding' with 'reproducible' data, but noting critical limitation that simulations 'never see full pore opening' only widening to ~4Å 'insufficient for rapid ion currents.'

Both address claims C24-C25 regarding AR domain compression and force distribution. OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as part of broader analysis (R1 covers C24-C29). Peer reviewers also find them SUPPORTED, noting this reproduces prior work and serves as foundation for novel force decomposition experiments.

Partial overlap on central model claims (C5, C22, C40, C57). OpenEval R6 finds the integrated central model SUPPORTED across claims C5-C6, C22-C23, C40, C57-C59. Peer R1 addresses subset of these (C5, C22, C34-C37, C39-C40, C57, C75) but rates as UNCERTAIN due to incomplete pore opening in simulations.

Partial overlap on central model claims (C6, C23, C59). OpenEval R6 finds the integrated model SUPPORTED including these claims. Peer R2 addresses C6, C23, C59 as part of compression-twist coupling findings and rates them SUPPORTED, treating them as supporting mechanistic details.

Both address functional robustness claims (C48, C66). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED based on demonstrated compression-twist coupling and force decomposition experiments. Peer reviewers also find them SUPPORTED as part of the broader torsional force transmission mechanism (addressed within their R2 evaluation).

Both address simulation limitations (C75). OpenEval finds C74-C75 SUPPORTED as appropriate acknowledgment of methodological limitations, noting short-timescale simulations can still reveal mechanistic trends. Peer reviewers include C75 in their UNCERTAIN evaluation of the main findings, with editor noting 'full opening of the channel is not seen' as a weakness.

OpenEval R11 addresses background knowledge claims C1-C2, C7-C16, finding them SUPPORTED as well-established context from prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background claims.

OpenEval R12 addresses claims C3-C4, C17-C21, C41-C42, C47, C60 that summarize prior work, finding them SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers did not separately evaluate literature summary claims. Peer R2 includes C47 but in context of novel compression-twist coupling findings.

OpenEval R13 addresses established knowledge claims C61, C67, C70 about TRP channels and MS channel mechanisms, finding them SUPPORTED as appropriate context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel contributions rather than contextual background claims.
